summary: The existing combined Infectum and Infectum-wa box contains one non-wa example and one Joseph quotation with two wa tokens. Counts are separated by example, not by number of repeated tokens.

The roof-rolling activity takes zero-marked roof NPs or -nne patient indexing, and b- marks the roller instrument. A possible denominal association with manduriye remains the inherited etymological question, not an established derivation.
mandinanne beside mandrínanne is retained exactly; it is not independently established as a dialectal sound rule. No new idiomatic phrase is required.

nḏərwola has the active Preterit-wa shape with L-agent -la; its anterior interpretation follows the narrative of an already vowed child before the journey to the festival. The English relative “whom” is not proof of a formally relative Turoyo construction; the Turoyo has the child NP followed by the predicate.

The new I sense is independent of round-1 III.1 rolling, whose broader felt/roof gloss remains unchanged. No etymological relationship between them is established. The inherited manduriye etymology is applicable to rolling, not evidence for dedication.

Permitted lookups: entry nḏr returned no entry; entry nḏ̣r describes erblicken, sehen, anschauen with Preterit Intransitive, not vow/dedicate; form nḏər gives consonantal candidates only. These results support an editorial root/homonym question rather than an automatic merger. No new Idiomatic phrase: a compositional verb with l-recipient, without a light verb or fixed noun combination.
Is r-less mandinanne at 94/24 a spoken contraction or textual omission?
Does mandrole in 58/278 designate rolling as in felt-making, or a more specific compacting operation?
The inherited stem note II: mxamele/mxaməl appears unrelated to ndr and may have been carried in with the Joseph quotation. Should it be moved to the relevant entry?

Confirm nḏərwola as “she had vowed/dedicated him” and elicit the Preterit/Infectum base pair; only the suffixed Preterit-wa is attested here, so the proposed Preterit base is explicitly reconstructed and the Infectum is left unestablished.
Should I “geloben, weihen” be published as a separate nḏr/ndr homonym rather than alongside III mandalle/mandər? Do not extend the inherited manduriye etymology to I without evidence.
A wrapped person can be rolled as felt is worked. The same rolling operation extends beyond roofs; the gloss is widened without a separate numbered sense.
